Statement (registered sorry body, not evidence): If iteratedFDeriv 2 f is differentiable and |D^3 f(W)[U,V,X]| <= s||U|| ||V|| ||X||, then |D^2 f(W + tau D)[D,D] - D^2 f(W)[D,D]| <= s ||D||^3 tau for tau >= 0. True by the mean value theorem: tau |-> D^2 f(W + tau D)[D,D] is differentiable with derivative D^3 f(W + tau D)[D,D,D] (iteratedFDeriv 2 f W ![U,V] = D^2 f(W)[U][V] and iteratedFDeriv 3 f W ![U,V,X] = D^3 f(W)[U][V][X] hold for every f, since iteratedFDeriv is fderiv composed with linear isometric curry equivalences, which commute with fderiv unconditionally).

Statement (registered sorry body, not evidence): Under three-fold differentiability (f, fderiv f, iteratedFDeriv 2 f differentiable) and the third-derivative bound: f(W+D) <= f(W) + Df(W)[D] + D^2 f(W)[D,D]/2 + s||D||^3/6. True: psi(tau) = f(W + tau D) has psi' = Df(W+tau D)[D], psi'' = D^2 f(W+tau D)[D,D] <= psi''(0) + s||D||^3 tau (hessian_diff_bound); integrating twice gives the bound. This is the source's Taylor step with Lagrange remainder bounded via Assumption 4.7 (lines 720-724), stated as an upper bound (which is all the source uses).
